POWER EQUIPMENT RENTAL AGREEMENT

This Agreement is made and entered into this 15th day of October, 2025, by and between:

**PowerGrid Solutions Ltd.** (hereinafter referred to as "the Company"), a company duly incorporated under the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, with its registered office at Plot 14B, Industrial Crescent, Ikeja, Lagos State, represented by its Managing Director, Engr. Tunde Okafor, and

**Lagos Sound & Lights Festival Company** (hereinafter referred to as "the Client"), with its registered office at 3B Adeola Odeku Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, represented by its Head of Operations, Mrs. Funmilayo Adewale.

WHEREAS the Client is organising a music festival scheduled to take place at the Eko Atlantic City Grounds, Lagos, from 20th December 2025 to 28th December 2025, and requires temporary power supply equipment for the duration of the event;

WHEREAS the Company is in the business of supplying and maintaining power generation and distribution equipment, and has agreed to rent out certain equipment to the Client on the terms and conditions hereinafter stated;

NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the parties agree as follows:

**ARTICLE 1: EQUIPMENT**

1.1 The Company agrees to rent to the Client, and the Client agrees to rent from the Company, the following equipment (hereinafter referred to as "the Equipment"):

| Item No. | Description | Quantity |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | 500kVA Generator (Silent, Diesel, with Automatic Transfer Switch) | 2 |
| 2 | 200A Distribution Panel (3-phase, with breakers and metering) | 4 |
| 3 | 50m Power Cable (Armoured, 4-core, with connectors) | 10 |

1.2 The contract with PowerGrid Solutions Ltd. specifies contracted_power_equipment as 2 x 500kVA generators, 4 x 200A distribution panels, 10 x 50m cables. Record status: current. The Equipment shall be delivered, installed, and commissioned by the Company at the Festival Site.

1.3 The Equipment shall be in good working condition at the time of delivery. The Company warrants that the Equipment meets all applicable Nigerian safety standards and is suitable for the intended purpose.

**ARTICLE 2: DELIVERY AND INSTALLATION**

2.1 The Company shall deliver the Equipment to the Festival Site on or before 1st December 2025, at a time to be mutually agreed upon in writing.

2.2 Delivery shall be deemed complete upon the signing of a Delivery Note by an authorised representative of the Client. The Client shall provide adequate access and a secure storage area for the Equipment.

2.3 Installation and commissioning shall be carried out by Company technicians. The Client shall provide a point of connection for the distribution panels and shall ensure that all site electrical wiring beyond the distribution panels is compliant with relevant regulations.

**ARTICLE 3: TERM**

3.1 The term of this Agreement shall commence on 1st December 2025 and expire on 31st December 2025, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.

3.2 The Client may request an extension of the term by giving written notice to the Company at least seven (7) days before the expiry date. Any extension shall be subject to the Company's availability and shall be documented in a written addendum.

**ARTICLE 4: RENTAL FEES AND PAYMENT**

4.1 The total rental fee for the Equipment for the term shall be Eight Million, Five Hundred Thousand Naira (₦8,500,000.00) only, exclusive of Value Added Tax (VAT).

4.2 Payment shall be made as follows:
- 50% (Four Million, Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira, ₦4,250,000.00) as a mobilization fee upon execution of this Agreement.
- 30% (Two Million, Five Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira, ₦2,550,000.00) upon delivery and installation of the Equipment.
- 20% (One Million, Seven Hundred Thousand Naira, ₦1,700,000.00) upon completion of the event and demobilization of the Equipment.
**ARTICLE 5: OPERATION, FUEL AND MAINTENANCE**

5.1 The Company shall provide one (1) qualified technician to be present at the Festival Site for the duration of the Term, including during load-in, rehearsals, performances, and load-out. The technician shall be responsible for the daily operation, monitoring, and routine servicing of the Equipment.

5.2 The Client shall provide, at its own cost, all diesel fuel required for the generators. Fuel shall be of good quality and shall comply with the specifications set out in the Equipment Manual. The Company shall not be liable for any loss of power or interruption caused by the use of adulterated or substandard fuel.

5.3 The Client shall ensure that the fuel storage area is at least fifteen (15) metres from the generator compound and is equipped with fire extinguishers rated for Class B fires. The Client shall maintain a fuel log, which the Company's technician may inspect at any reasonable time.

5.4 Routine maintenance, including oil changes, filter replacement, and battery checks, shall be carried out by the Company's technician. The Company shall keep a maintenance log for the Equipment and shall make it available to the Client upon request.

5.5 The Client shall not, and shall ensure that its agents and contractors shall not, operate, adjust, repair, or tamper with the Equipment without the prior written consent of the Company. Any unauthorised interference with the Equipment shall void the warranties under this Agreement, and the Client shall be liable for all resulting damage.

5.6 In the event of a breakdown or malfunction of the Equipment, the Company shall use reasonable endeavours to repair or replace the affected unit within twenty-four (24) hours of notification by the Client. The Company shall provide a replacement unit of equivalent or better specification if the repair cannot be completed within that period.

5.7 The Company shall not be responsible for the failure of any equipment belonging to the Client or to third parties that is connected to the distribution panels, including but not limited to sound systems, lighting consoles, and catering appliances.

**ARTICLE 6: WARRANTIES**

6.1 The Company warrants that the Equipment is fit for the purpose of providing temporary power for the Festival and that it conforms to the specifications described in Schedule A. This warranty is valid for the duration of the Term.

6.2 The Company further warrants that the Equipment is free from defects in material and workmanship at the time of delivery. The Client's sole remedy for breach of this warranty shall be the repair or replacement of the defective Equipment at the Company's option.

6.3 Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, the Company makes no other warranties, whether express, implied, statutory, or otherwise, including any implied warranty of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.

**ARTICLE 7: INDEMNIFICATION**

7.1 The Client shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Company, its officers, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable legal fees) arising out of or in connection with:
(a) the use, operation, or handling of the Equipment by the Client or its contractors, except where such claims arise from the negligence or wilful misconduct of the Company;
(b) any breach of this Agreement by the Client; or
(c) any injury to persons or damage to property at the Festival Site, except to the extent caused by the negligence of the Company.

7.2 The Company shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Client from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses arising out of or in connection with the negligence or wilful misconduct of the Company's personnel in the performance of their duties under this Agreement.

Date of Publication: 1st December, 2025
Outage Date: Saturday, 6th December, 2025
Outage Time: 14:00 HRS to 16:00 HRS (2:00 PM – 4:00 PM WAT)
Affected Zones / Feeders: Feeder 24 (Alausa), Feeder 18 (Oregun), Feeder 22 (Mende), and Feeder 31 (Maryland) — see detailed list below.

The Management of Ikeja Electric Distribution Company (IKEDC) wishes to inform the general public, our esteemed customers, and all stakeholders within the Ikeja Business Unit of a scheduled maintenance outage on Saturday, 6th December, 2025. This planned interruption is necessary to carry out essential preventive maintenance on the 33kV switchgear at the Ikeja West Transmission Station, as well as the replacement of two faulty distribution transformers and the inspection of high-tension insulators along the affected feeders.

The scheduled maintenance outage will commence at 14:00 HRS and is expected to be completed by 16:00 HRS. Ikeja Electric Distribution Company announced a scheduled_maintenance_outage from 2025-12-06 14:00 to 16:00 WAT. Record status: current. During this two-hour window, power supply will be interrupted to the areas listed in the table below. Please note that restoration may occur before the stated time if the maintenance is completed ahead of schedule. In the event of any unforeseen delay, an update will be provided via our official social media channels and SMS alerts.

AREAS AFFECTED BY THE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE OUTAGE:

| S/N | Feeder / Substation | Affected Areas / Streets | Est. Number of Customers |
|-----|---------------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | Feeder 24 – Alausa | Alausa Central Business District, Government House (partial), Alausa Secretariat (partial), Oko-Oba Road, Adeola Odeku Street (part), Obafemi Awolowo Way (part) | 1,850 |
| 2 | Feeder 18 – Oregun | Oregun Industrial Estate, Oregun Road, Adebowale Street, Oshifila Street, Omididun Street, Olu-Osho Street, Kudirat Abiola Way (part) | 2,400 |
| 3 | Feeder 22 – Mende | Mende Estate, Mende Road, Abimbola Street, Adeola Street, Oke-Ira Road (part), Fola Osibo Road (part) | 1,720 |
| 4 | Feeder 31 – Maryland | Maryland Junction (part), Ikorodu Road (part – from Maryland to Anthony), Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) (partial), Ladipo Oluwole Street, Gbaja Street, Ogunbiyi Street | 2,150 |

TOTAL ESTIMATED AFFECTED CUSTOMERS: 8,120

PURPOSE OF THE MAINTENANCE:

1. Replacement of two (2) faulty 500kVA distribution transformers at Oregun and Mende substations.
2. Routine inspection and replacement of damaged high-tension insulators on the 11kV lines along Feeder 24 and Feeder 31.
3. Servicing of the 33kV circuit breaker at the Ikeja West Transmission Station (joint exercise with TCN engineers).
4. Vegetation clearing along the right-of-way of Feeder 18 and Feeder 22 to prevent future faults caused by tree branches.

IMPORTANT NOTES FOR CUSTOMERS:

- Customers are advised to switch off all electrical appliances before the maintenance period begins and to keep them switched off until power supply is fully restored. This is to protect your appliances from voltage surges that may occur during restoration.
- Businesses that rely on continuous power supply (e.g., cold rooms, data centers, banks, and medical facilities) are strongly advised to make adequate backup arrangements for the two-hour period.
- The scheduled maintenance will NOT affect the following areas: Ikeja GRA (Feeder 12), Computer Village (Feeder 15), and Ogba (Feeder 27). These feeders will be supplied from an alternative source during the period.
- Customers on the affected feeders who have prepaid meters are advised that no billing adjustment is required for the two-hour interruption, as the meters will simply not record consumption during the outage period.
PLEASE READ CAREFULLY – SAFETY AND PREPARATION GUIDANCE FOR THE SCHEDULED OUTAGE

Dear Esteemed Customers,

Further to our earlier notice regarding the scheduled maintenance outage on Sunday, 7th December 2025, from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m., we wish to provide additional guidance to help you prepare adequately and ensure your safety during the exercise. The maintenance will affect the feeders and areas listed in our previous communication, and we encourage all customers in the affected zones to take note of the following instructions.

HOW TO PREPARE FOR THE OUTAGE

1. Charge Your Devices: Please ensure that your mobile phones, laptops, power banks, and other essential electronic devices are fully charged before 8:00 a.m. on the day of the outage. This will help you stay connected and informed during the two-hour period.

2. Store Water: If you rely on electric pumps for your water supply, we advise you to store enough water in clean containers before the outage begins. This is particularly important for households and businesses in the Oregun, Mende, and Maryland areas.

3. Preserve Perishables: For customers with cold rooms, refrigerators, and freezers, please minimize the opening of these appliances during the outage to preserve the cold temperature. Perishable items such as meat, fish, and dairy products should be kept in the coldest part of the appliance. If you have a generator, you may wish to run it intermittently to keep your cold room operational, especially if you store medical supplies or other temperature-sensitive items.

4. Backup Power Arrangements: Businesses that rely on continuous power supply — including cold rooms, data centers, banks, and medical facilities — are strongly advised to have adequate backup arrangements in place. Please test your generators and ensure you have sufficient fuel before the maintenance period. For data centers and medical facilities, we recommend that you also verify your UPS and inverter systems are functioning properly.

5. Security Lighting: If you depend on electric lighting for security purposes, please make arrangements for alternative lighting, such as rechargeable lamps, solar lights, or candles. Ensure that any candles are placed in safe holders and kept away from flammable materials.

6. Prepare Your Generator: If you plan to use a generator during the outage, please check the fuel level, oil level, and coolant in advance. Run the generator outdoors or in a well-ventilated area to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning. Never operate a generator inside your home, garage, or any enclosed space.

7. Unplug Sensitive Equipment: We strongly advise that you unplug computers, televisions, microwaves, and other sensitive electronic equipment before the maintenance begins. This will protect them from voltage surges that may occur when power is restored. If you have a surge protector, ensure that it is in good working condition.

SAFETY TIPS DURING THE OUTAGE

- Treat all electrical wires and equipment as live, even during the outage. Do not touch any fallen wires or poles. If you see a fallen wire, please keep your distance and report it immediately to our emergency line.

- Do not attempt to carry out any repairs on your electrical installation during the outage. Only certified electricians should work on electrical systems, and they must ensure that the main switch is off before commencing any work.

- If you use a generator, ensure that it is properly connected through a changeover switch. Do not connect your generator directly to a wall socket, as this can cause back-feeding, which is dangerous to our engineers working on the lines and to your own appliances.

- Keep children and pets away from electrical installations, including distribution transformers, substations, and meter boxes. These areas are not playgrounds.

Archive item 4: Incident Report: Main Stage Power Outage
Source format: incident report

No injuries were reported. No equipment damage was confirmed at the time of writing. The incident caused a delay to the festival running order of approximately two hours. The full schedule for the remainder of Day 2 was revised and communicated to all stakeholders.

SECTION 2: TIMELINE OF EVENTS

All times listed are West Africa Time (WAT). Times are based on the Operations Desk log, stage manager radio logs, and witness statements.

| Time (WAT) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 14:55 | Stage A fully powered. Sound check for DJ Kemi completed. G1 running normally, load at 62%. G2 on standby, auto-start enabled. |
| 15:00 | DJ Kemi set begins. Power stable. |
| 15:28 | Stage manager reports slight flicker on console display screens. No action taken, attributed to minor voltage fluctuation. |
| 15:30 | Total loss of power at Main Stage. All stage equipment goes dark. Stage manager calls Operations Desk by radio. |
| 15:31 | Operations Desk receives call. Technician dispatched to generator compound. |
| 15:33 | G1 confirmed shut down. Visual inspection shows no obvious fault; fuel gauge reading not recorded due to technician priority on restart. |
| 15:35 | G2 auto-start fails to engage. Technician begins manual start procedure. |
| 15:40 | G2 manual start unsuccessful. Fault indicated on control panel – low coolant alarm. |
| 15:45 | DJ Kemi set officially abandoned. Crowd management team notified. Announcement made to audience regarding technical difficulty. |
| 15:50 | Technician begins troubleshooting G2 coolant system. |
| 16:05 | Operations Manager authorizes connection of portable rental generator (G3) to Main Stage distribution board. |
| 16:20 | G3 arrives on site from festival storage yard. |
| 16:35 | G3 positioned and cabling run to Main Stage distribution board. |
| 16:50 | G3 connection completed. Load test initiated. |
| 17:05 | Load test successful. Stage systems powered up sequentially. |
| 17:15 | Sound console and monitor systems fully operational. |
| 17:45 | Power fully restored to Main Stage. All systems confirmed online. Stage manager gives go-ahead for revised schedule. |
| 18:00 | Revised running order begins with next scheduled artist. |

The incident report states Main Stage power_outage_start_time occurred at 2025-12-06 15:30 WAT. Record status: historical.

SECTION 3: DETAILED INCIDENT DESCRIPTION

The Main Stage (Stage A) is the primary performance area of the Lagos Soundwave Festival. It is supplied by a dedicated power distribution network fed from the festival's generator compound, located approximately 85 metres from the stage. The compound houses two primary generator sets: G1 (500 kVA, diesel) and G2 (500 kVA, diesel, auto-start standby). Both units are owned by the festival and maintained under contract by PowerGrid Services (PGS). A third generator (G3, 350 kVA) is a rental unit held on site for contingency use.

At 15:30 WAT, the Main Stage lost all power. The outage was instantaneous, with no preceding gradual degradation reported by the stage crew. The stage manager, Mr. Tunde Adeyemi, stated that the console displays flickered briefly at approximately 15:28, but this was not considered significant at the time. The sound engineer on duty, Miss Chiamaka Okafor, confirmed that the flicker lasted less than two seconds and did not affect audio output.

The failure of G1 was confirmed by the duty technician, Mr. Emeka Nwosu, who reached the generator compound at approximately 15:33. G1 had shut down completely. The control panel indicated an unspecified fault code. Mr. Nwosu reported that the fuel gauge was not readable at the time of his inspection due to the urgency of the situation, and he prioritized attempting to bring G2 online.
Meanwhile, the stage manager (Mr. Tunde Adeyemi) had been informed of the outage at 15:35. He consulted the festival’s operations coordinator, Ms. Funmilayo Bakare, and together they reviewed the contingency plan. The decision was made at 15:42 to move all artist changeovers and sound checks to the secondary stage (Stage B) for the interim, and to place the Main Stage program on hold. This decision was communicated to the artist liaison team at 15:45. The revised running order, which was later issued at 17:50, incorporated this hold.

At 15:50, Mr. Nwosu and his assistant, Mr. Ibrahim Suleiman, began inspecting the distribution path from the generator compound to the Main Stage. They first checked the main feeder cable at the compound end. The cable was visually intact, and insulation testing showed no earth fault. They then proceeded to the distribution board at the stage end, arriving at approximately 16:05. On opening the board, they found that the main incoming breaker (800 A) had tripped. The breaker’s trip flag indicated a short-circuit condition, not an overload. Mr. Nwosu reset the breaker and attempted to close it, but it immediately tripped again.

At 16:10, they isolated the board from the generator side and began testing the outgoing feeders one by one. The feeder to the stage lighting dimmer racks tested clear. The feeder to the sound system power distribution unit (PDU) tested clear. The feeder to the back-of-house (BOH) services, which supplies lighting for the artist holding area and dressing rooms, also tested clear. The fourth feeder, which supplies the stage sub-distribution board (located under the stage deck), showed a low insulation reading of 0.2 MΩ, well below the acceptable threshold of 1 MΩ. This indicated a fault on that feeder or on equipment connected to it.

According to the report, Main Stage power_restored_time was 2025-12-06 17:45 WAT. Record status: historical.

At 16:20, Mr. Nwosu and Mr. Suleiman isolated the stage sub-distribution board by opening its main isolator at the board itself. They then re-tested the feeder from the main board; the reading improved to above 50 MΩ, confirming that the fault was downstream of the isolator, on the stage sub-distribution board side. They opened the sub-distribution board at 16:25. Inside, they found evidence of water ingress: moisture on the busbars, slight corrosion on the terminals of the neutral link, and a small amount of standing water in the bottom of the enclosure. The board is located in a recess under the stage deck, and the deck had been pressure-washed earlier that morning as part of routine cleaning. The water ingress had evidently occurred during or after the washing, and the fault had developed when the load was applied.

Mr. Nwosu’s log entry for 16:25 reads: “Sub-dist board wet. Busbars corroded. Neutral link terminal rust. Water in bottom of enclosure. Fault likely short between phase and neutral under load.”

At 16:30, the decision was made to bypass the faulty sub-distribution board. The stage sub-distribution board supplies power to the monitor amplifier racks, the stage power outlets (used by the band and by stage crew equipment), and the front-of-house (FOH) power feed. The FOH feed, however, is not routed through the sub-distribution board; it is a direct feed from the main distribution board. This meant that the FOH console and the main PA system could be powered independently of the faulty board.

At 16:35, Ms. Bakare approved the bypass plan. The plan was to run a temporary cable directly from the main distribution board to the monitor amplifier racks, using a spare 63 A feeder that had been pre-installed for the festival’s video wall (which was not in use at the time). The monitor racks were reconnected at 16:45. The stage power outlets were left isolated, and the stage crew was instructed to use battery-powered tools and to run extension leads from the BOH supply for any essential equipment. The artist liaison team was informed that stage power outlets would be unavailable for the remainder of the day.
# INCIDENT REPORT: MAIN STAGE POWER OUTAGE

**Incident Reference No:** LSW/IR/2025/0142  
**Date of Incident:** 7 December 2025  
**Report Compiled:** 8 December 2025  
**Compiled By:** T. Adeyemi, Operations Coordinator  
**Approved By:** N. Bakare, Festival Director

---

## 8. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

### 8.1 Direct Cause
The immediate cause of the power outage at the Main Stage was a phase-to-neutral short circuit within the stage sub-distribution board, resulting from water ingress into the enclosure. The short occurred when the board was placed under load at approximately 16:10. The fault manifested as a loud bang from the board enclosure, tripping the upstream circuit breaker on the main distribution board and cutting power to the monitor amplifier racks, stage power outlets, and stage lighting.

### 8.2 Contributory Factors

**a) Pressure Washing of Stage Deck**
The stage deck was pressure-washed at approximately 09:30 on the morning of the incident as part of routine cleaning. The sub-distribution board is located in a recess beneath the stage deck. The enclosure is rated IP54, which provides protection against splashing water but not against direct water jets or prolonged immersion. The pressure washer used by the cleaning crew was rated at 150 bar, well above the manufacturer's recommended maximum for cleaning near electrical enclosures. The cleaning crew was not aware of the board's location and did not take any precautions to protect it.

**b) Inadequate Sealing of Cable Entries**
Upon inspection of the sub-distribution board, it was noted that the cable glands at the top of the enclosure were not fully tightened. The glands had also not been sealed with the recommended silicone compound. This allowed water to run down the cables and into the enclosure. The cable entries were identified as the most probable point of ingress, given that the enclosure door seals appeared intact and showed no signs of deterioration.

**c) Lack of Routine Inspection**
The sub-distribution board had not been included in the pre-event electrical inspection checklist. The inspection checklist, which was completed on 5 December 2025, covered the main distribution board, the generator sets, and the FOH power feed, but did not include the stage sub-distribution board. This omission was due to an oversight in the checklist preparation; the stage sub-distribution board was not listed in the festival's asset register at the time the checklist was drafted.

**d) Absence of RCD Protection**
The stage sub-distribution board was not protected by a residual current device (RCD). The upstream breaker on the main distribution board was a standard moulded case circuit breaker (MCCB) rated at 100 A, which provides overcurrent protection but does not detect earth leakage. An RCD would have tripped earlier upon detection of the leakage current caused by the water ingress, potentially preventing the phase-to-neutral short and the resulting damage.

**e) Communication Gaps Between Departments**
The cleaning crew that performed the pressure washing was engaged by the venue management and was not under the direct supervision of the festival's technical team. There was no formal procedure for coordinating cleaning activities with the electrical department. The cleaning crew did not receive any briefing regarding the location of electrical equipment beneath the stage deck.

### 8.3 Coincidental and Non-Contributory Factors

**a) Generator Set G1 Fuel Pressure Reading**
At approximately 15:55, the generator set operator, Mr. S. Okafor, recorded a low fuel pressure reading on G1. This reading was noted in the generator log and initially raised concerns that the generator might have been contributing to the power issue. However, subsequent investigation confirmed that the fuel pressure reading was due to a faulty sensor on the fuel filter housing. The sensor was replaced on 8 December 2025, and the reading returned to normal. G1 was operating within normal parameters at the time of the incident and did not contribute to the outage.

documents.title: Public Notice of Scheduled Maintenance Outage
documents.content:
PLEASE READ CAREFULLY – SAFETY AND PREPARATION GUIDANCE FOR THE SCHEDULED OUTAGE

Dear Esteemed Customers,

Further to our earlier notice regarding the scheduled maintenance outage on Sunday, 7th December 2025, from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m., we wish to provide additional guidance to help you prepare adequately and ensure your safety during the exercise. The maintenance will affect the feeders and areas listed in our previous communication, and we encourage all customers in the affected zones to take note of the following instructions.

HOW TO PREPARE FOR THE OUTAGE

1. Charge Your Devices: Please ensure that your mobile phones, laptops, power banks, and other essential electronic devices are fully charged before 8:00 a.m. on the day of the outage. This will help you stay connected and informed during the two-hour period.

2. Store Water: If you rely on electric pumps for your water supply, we advise you to store enough water in clean containers before the outage begins. This is particularly important for households and businesses in the Oregun, Mende, and Maryland areas.

3. Preserve Perishables: For customers with cold rooms, refrigerators, and freezers, please minimize the opening of these appliances during the outage to preserve the cold temperature. Perishable items such as meat, fish, and dairy products should be kept in the coldest part of the appliance. If you have a generator, you may wish to run it intermittently to keep your cold room operational, especially if you store medical supplies or other temperature-sensitive items.

4. Backup Power Arrangements: Businesses that rely on continuous power supply — including cold rooms, data centers, banks, and medical facilities — are strongly advised to have adequate backup arrangements in place. Please test your generators and ensure you have sufficient fuel before the maintenance period. For data centers and medical facilities, we recommend that you also verify your UPS and inverter systems are functioning properly.

5. Security Lighting: If you depend on electric lighting for security purposes, please make arrangements for alternative lighting, such as rechargeable lamps, solar lights, or candles. Ensure that any candles are placed in safe holders and kept away from flammable materials.

6. Prepare Your Generator: If you plan to use a generator during the outage, please check the fuel level, oil level, and coolant in advance. Run the generator outdoors or in a well-ventilated area to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning. Never operate a generator inside your home, garage, or any enclosed space.

7. Unplug Sensitive Equipment: We strongly advise that you unplug computers, televisions, microwaves, and other sensitive electronic equipment before the maintenance begins. This will protect them from voltage surges that may occur when power is restored. If you have a surge protector, ensure that it is in good working condition.

SAFETY TIPS DURING THE OUTAGE

- Treat all electrical wires and equipment as live, even during the outage. Do not touch any fallen wires or poles. If you see a fallen wire, please keep your distance and report it immediately to our emergency line.

- Do not attempt to carry out any repairs on your electrical installation during the outage. Only certified electricians should work on electrical systems, and they must ensure that the main switch is off before commencing any work.

- If you use a generator, ensure that it is properly connected through a changeover switch. Do not connect your generator directly to a wall socket, as this can cause back-feeding, which is dangerous to our engineers working on the lines and to your own appliances.

- Keep children and pets away from electrical installations, including distribution transformers, substations, and meter boxes. These areas are not playgrounds.

documents.title: Incident Report: Main Stage Power Outage
documents.content:
No injuries were reported. No equipment damage was confirmed at the time of writing. The incident caused a delay to the festival running order of approximately two hours. The full schedule for the remainder of Day 2 was revised and communicated to all stakeholders.

SECTION 2: TIMELINE OF EVENTS

All times listed are West Africa Time (WAT). Times are based on the Operations Desk log, stage manager radio logs, and witness statements.

| Time (WAT) | Event |
|------------|-------|
| 14:55 | Stage A fully powered. Sound check for DJ Kemi completed. G1 running normally, load at 62%. G2 on standby, auto-start enabled. |
| 15:00 | DJ Kemi set begins. Power stable. |
| 15:28 | Stage manager reports slight flicker on console display screens. No action taken, attributed to minor voltage fluctuation. |
| 15:30 | Total loss of power at Main Stage. All stage equipment goes dark. Stage manager calls Operations Desk by radio. |
| 15:31 | Operations Desk receives call. Technician dispatched to generator compound. |
| 15:33 | G1 confirmed shut down. Visual inspection shows no obvious fault; fuel gauge reading not recorded due to technician priority on restart. |
| 15:35 | G2 auto-start fails to engage. Technician begins manual start procedure. |
| 15:40 | G2 manual start unsuccessful. Fault indicated on control panel – low coolant alarm. |
| 15:45 | DJ Kemi set officially abandoned. Crowd management team notified. Announcement made to audience regarding technical difficulty. |
| 15:50 | Technician begins troubleshooting G2 coolant system. |
| 16:05 | Operations Manager authorizes connection of portable rental generator (G3) to Main Stage distribution board. |
| 16:20 | G3 arrives on site from festival storage yard. |
| 16:35 | G3 positioned and cabling run to Main Stage distribution board. |
| 16:50 | G3 connection completed. Load test initiated. |
| 17:05 | Load test successful. Stage systems powered up sequentially. |
| 17:15 | Sound console and monitor systems fully operational. |
| 17:45 | Power fully restored to Main Stage. All systems confirmed online. Stage manager gives go-ahead for revised schedule. |
| 18:00 | Revised running order begins with next scheduled artist. |

The incident report states Main Stage power_outage_start_time occurred at 2025-12-06 15:30 WAT. Record status: historical.

SECTION 3: DETAILED INCIDENT DESCRIPTION

The Main Stage (Stage A) is the primary performance area of the Lagos Soundwave Festival. It is supplied by a dedicated power distribution network fed from the festival's generator compound, located approximately 85 metres from the stage. The compound houses two primary generator sets: G1 (500 kVA, diesel) and G2 (500 kVA, diesel, auto-start standby). Both units are owned by the festival and maintained under contract by PowerGrid Services (PGS). A third generator (G3, 350 kVA) is a rental unit held on site for contingency use.

At 15:30 WAT, the Main Stage lost all power. The outage was instantaneous, with no preceding gradual degradation reported by the stage crew. The stage manager, Mr. Tunde Adeyemi, stated that the console displays flickered briefly at approximately 15:28, but this was not considered significant at the time. The sound engineer on duty, Miss Chiamaka Okafor, confirmed that the flicker lasted less than two seconds and did not affect audio output.

The failure of G1 was confirmed by the duty technician, Mr. Emeka Nwosu, who reached the generator compound at approximately 15:33. G1 had shut down completely. The control panel indicated an unspecified fault code. Mr. Nwosu reported that the fuel gauge was not readable at the time of his inspection due to the urgency of the situation, and he prioritized attempting to bring G2 online.

documents.title: Incident Report: Main Stage Power Outage
documents.content:
Meanwhile, the stage manager (Mr. Tunde Adeyemi) had been informed of the outage at 15:35. He consulted the festival’s operations coordinator, Ms. Funmilayo Bakare, and together they reviewed the contingency plan. The decision was made at 15:42 to move all artist changeovers and sound checks to the secondary stage (Stage B) for the interim, and to place the Main Stage program on hold. This decision was communicated to the artist liaison team at 15:45. The revised running order, which was later issued at 17:50, incorporated this hold.

At 15:50, Mr. Nwosu and his assistant, Mr. Ibrahim Suleiman, began inspecting the distribution path from the generator compound to the Main Stage. They first checked the main feeder cable at the compound end. The cable was visually intact, and insulation testing showed no earth fault. They then proceeded to the distribution board at the stage end, arriving at approximately 16:05. On opening the board, they found that the main incoming breaker (800 A) had tripped. The breaker’s trip flag indicated a short-circuit condition, not an overload. Mr. Nwosu reset the breaker and attempted to close it, but it immediately tripped again.

At 16:10, they isolated the board from the generator side and began testing the outgoing feeders one by one. The feeder to the stage lighting dimmer racks tested clear. The feeder to the sound system power distribution unit (PDU) tested clear. The feeder to the back-of-house (BOH) services, which supplies lighting for the artist holding area and dressing rooms, also tested clear. The fourth feeder, which supplies the stage sub-distribution board (located under the stage deck), showed a low insulation reading of 0.2 MΩ, well below the acceptable threshold of 1 MΩ. This indicated a fault on that feeder or on equipment connected to it.

According to the report, Main Stage power_restored_time was 2025-12-06 17:45 WAT. Record status: historical.

At 16:20, Mr. Nwosu and Mr. Suleiman isolated the stage sub-distribution board by opening its main isolator at the board itself. They then re-tested the feeder from the main board; the reading improved to above 50 MΩ, confirming that the fault was downstream of the isolator, on the stage sub-distribution board side. They opened the sub-distribution board at 16:25. Inside, they found evidence of water ingress: moisture on the busbars, slight corrosion on the terminals of the neutral link, and a small amount of standing water in the bottom of the enclosure. The board is located in a recess under the stage deck, and the deck had been pressure-washed earlier that morning as part of routine cleaning. The water ingress had evidently occurred during or after the washing, and the fault had developed when the load was applied.

Mr. Nwosu’s log entry for 16:25 reads: “Sub-dist board wet. Busbars corroded. Neutral link terminal rust. Water in bottom of enclosure. Fault likely short between phase and neutral under load.”

At 16:30, the decision was made to bypass the faulty sub-distribution board. The stage sub-distribution board supplies power to the monitor amplifier racks, the stage power outlets (used by the band and by stage crew equipment), and the front-of-house (FOH) power feed. The FOH feed, however, is not routed through the sub-distribution board; it is a direct feed from the main distribution board. This meant that the FOH console and the main PA system could be powered independently of the faulty board.

At 16:35, Ms. Bakare approved the bypass plan. The plan was to run a temporary cable directly from the main distribution board to the monitor amplifier racks, using a spare 63 A feeder that had been pre-installed for the festival’s video wall (which was not in use at the time). The monitor racks were reconnected at 16:45. The stage power outlets were left isolated, and the stage crew was instructed to use battery-powered tools and to run extension leads from the BOH supply for any essential equipment. The artist liaison team was informed that stage power outlets would be unavailable for the remainder of the day.

# INCIDENT REPORT: MAIN STAGE POWER OUTAGE

**Incident Reference No:** LSW/IR/2025/0142  
**Date of Incident:** 7 December 2025  
**Report Compiled:** 8 December 2025  
**Compiled By:** T. Adeyemi, Operations Coordinator  
**Approved By:** N. Bakare, Festival Director

---

## 8. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS

### 8.1 Direct Cause
The immediate cause of the power outage at the Main Stage was a phase-to-neutral short circuit within the stage sub-distribution board, resulting from water ingress into the enclosure. The short occurred when the board was placed under load at approximately 16:10. The fault manifested as a loud bang from the board enclosure, tripping the upstream circuit breaker on the main distribution board and cutting power to the monitor amplifier racks, stage power outlets, and stage lighting.

### 8.2 Contributory Factors

**a) Pressure Washing of Stage Deck**
The stage deck was pressure-washed at approximately 09:30 on the morning of the incident as part of routine cleaning. The sub-distribution board is located in a recess beneath the stage deck. The enclosure is rated IP54, which provides protection against splashing water but not against direct water jets or prolonged immersion. The pressure washer used by the cleaning crew was rated at 150 bar, well above the manufacturer's recommended maximum for cleaning near electrical enclosures. The cleaning crew was not aware of the board's location and did not take any precautions to protect it.

**b) Inadequate Sealing of Cable Entries**
Upon inspection of the sub-distribution board, it was noted that the cable glands at the top of the enclosure were not fully tightened. The glands had also not been sealed with the recommended silicone compound. This allowed water to run down the cables and into the enclosure. The cable entries were identified as the most probable point of ingress, given that the enclosure door seals appeared intact and showed no signs of deterioration.

**c) Lack of Routine Inspection**
The sub-distribution board had not been included in the pre-event electrical inspection checklist. The inspection checklist, which was completed on 5 December 2025, covered the main distribution board, the generator sets, and the FOH power feed, but did not include the stage sub-distribution board. This omission was due to an oversight in the checklist preparation; the stage sub-distribution board was not listed in the festival's asset register at the time the checklist was drafted.

**d) Absence of RCD Protection**
The stage sub-distribution board was not protected by a residual current device (RCD). The upstream breaker on the main distribution board was a standard moulded case circuit breaker (MCCB) rated at 100 A, which provides overcurrent protection but does not detect earth leakage. An RCD would have tripped earlier upon detection of the leakage current caused by the water ingress, potentially preventing the phase-to-neutral short and the resulting damage.

**e) Communication Gaps Between Departments**
The cleaning crew that performed the pressure washing was engaged by the venue management and was not under the direct supervision of the festival's technical team. There was no formal procedure for coordinating cleaning activities with the electrical department. The cleaning crew did not receive any briefing regarding the location of electrical equipment beneath the stage deck.

### 8.3 Coincidental and Non-Contributory Factors

**a) Generator Set G1 Fuel Pressure Reading**
At approximately 15:55, the generator set operator, Mr. S. Okafor, recorded a low fuel pressure reading on G1. This reading was noted in the generator log and initially raised concerns that the generator might have been contributing to the power issue. However, subsequent investigation confirmed that the fuel pressure reading was due to a faulty sensor on the fuel filter housing. The sensor was replaced on 8 December 2025, and the reading returned to normal. G1 was operating within normal parameters at the time of the incident and did not contribute to the outage.
